evals.name: full-portfolio-architecture-signal
evals.prompt:
Document the Python library at /Users/vbezdek/Work/skillstack/benchmarks/documentation-generator/fixtures/slugify-utils/

Read the source files first (use Bash ls and Read tools on the fixture path). Then generate the full documentation portfolio. Apply all phases of your documentation workflow. Save every output file to the CURRENT directory. Print the list of files you created at the end.
evals.expected_output: Multi-file portfolio including architecture.md, dedicated error/exception reference, and at least 6 total docs.
expectations: A file named 'architecture.md' or 'ARCHITECTURE.md' (at root or in a docs/ subdirectory) exists in the output. It must describe the system's module structure, component relationships, or key design decisions of the slugify-utils library. A generic README or API reference does NOT satisfy this — the file must be specifically about architecture, module organization, or system design.

At least one output file contains a module responsibilities table or component overview that maps each of the library's three main modules (core.py, validators.py, languages.py) to its responsibility or role. The table or list must name all three modules. A generic description of what the library does does NOT satisfy this — it must be a structured per-module breakdown. This content typically lives in architecture.md or a similar architectural overview.

The documentation output contains AT LEAST 5 distinct markdown files (counting docs/ subdirectory files). A portfolio of only README + CHANGELOG (2-3 files) does NOT satisfy this — the full-portfolio prompt targets comprehensive coverage.

evals.name: api-and-troubleshooting-coverage
evals.prompt:
Read the Python library at /Users/vbezdek/Work/skillstack/benchmarks/documentation-generator/fixtures/slugify-utils/ and generate its API reference documentation.

Read core.py, validators.py, and languages.py first using Read or Bash tools. Then produce: (1) a complete API reference for all public functions, (2) a quickstart guide, and (3) a troubleshooting guide. Save all output to the CURRENT directory. Print the list of files at the end.
evals.expected_output: API reference covering all 5 public functions with exception tables; quickstart with multilingual examples; troubleshooting with error-to-cause mapping.
expectations: The troubleshooting or error guide contains a table OR structured list mapping at least 3 error conditions to their causes or fixes, where entries specifically reference SlugError or ValueError (the actual exceptions in the codebase). A generic 'check your input' section without named exception types does NOT satisfy this.

The API reference documents ALL FIVE of these public symbols: slugify, unslugify, batch_slugify, validate_slug, is_valid_slug. Each must appear as a named section heading or function entry. Missing any of the five does NOT satisfy this.

The quickstart or getting-started file contains code examples for AT LEAST 2 different supported languages — for example, a Russian (lang='ru') AND a Czech or German example, demonstrating the multilingual capability. A quickstart with only English examples does NOT satisfy this.

evals.name: architecture-and-contributor-docs
evals.prompt:
Read the Python library at /Users/vbezdek/Work/skillstack/benchmarks/documentation-generator/fixtures/slugify-utils/ and produce its architecture and contributor documentation.

Read all source files. Then produce: (1) an architecture decision record (ADR) explaining the design decision to keep transliteration tables in a separate languages.py module, (2) a contributor guide, and (3) a documentation gap register. Save all files to the CURRENT directory. Print the list of files at the end.
evals.expected_output: ADR with Context + Decision + Consequences headings; CONTRIBUTING.md with setup/style/PR sections; gap register with specific numbered gaps.
expectations: The ADR file contains 'Context', 'Decision', AND 'Consequences' as markdown headings (##, ###, or bold heading — any heading style). All three must be present in the same file. An ADR with only Context and Decision but no Consequences does NOT satisfy this.

A contributor guide or CONTRIBUTING.md file exists covering ALL THREE of: (a) how to set up a local development environment (clone + install steps), (b) code style or formatting requirements, AND (c) how to submit a pull request or change. A CONTRIBUTING.md covering only 1 or 2 of these three areas does NOT satisfy this.

A gap register, 'Documentation Gaps', or 'Known Gaps' file exists with AT LEAST 5 specific named gaps (not just headers). Each gap must describe a missing or incomplete piece of documentation. A gap register with only 1-2 entries or only high-level categories does NOT satisfy this.
